title: Sinus pause or arrest
summary: The sinus node fails to fire for a while. No P wave and no QRS appear until it, or a lower pacemaker, restarts.

events.label: Regular beats
events.caption: The sinus node fires regularly at first, about 75 times a minute.
events.ecg: Normal P waves and QRS complexes.

events.label: Pause
events.caption: Then it fails to fire. A short failure is a pause; a longer one is sinus arrest. Nothing is activated.
events.ecg: A long flat line with no P wave and no QRS.

events.label: Node restarts
events.caption: The node starts again. If it did not, a lower pacemaker would eventually take over as an escape rhythm.
events.ecg: Normal P wave and QRS resume.

teaching_points: A sinus pause or arrest is a failure of sinus node automaticity: no P wave appears where one is expected (slide 26).
A pause that is an exact multiple of the usual P-P interval suggests sinoatrial exit block instead (slide 25).
Symptoms depend on how long it lasts: dizziness, loss of consciousness (slide 16).
